questions.key_step: Locate the centre of similitude, tangents, and the circle through the four contact points (centre on the x-axis by symmetry).
questions.justification: Four chained computations (tangents, contact points, C3, chord); option-based so checkable, but the arithmetic is heavy. Comparable to a long routine circle chain with one symmetry insight.

questions.key_step: Running maximum of a piecewise g: flat after the peak, and a corner only where g regains the peak with non-zero slope.
questions.justification: Needs the shape of g, the point 4+sqrt2 where the old peak is regained, and slope tests at 2, 4+sqrt2 and 6; options contain tempting wrong sets, but it is standard.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2023-P2-Q6 (L4, MCQ; easier as SCQ with options)

questions.key_step: Radical centre moves on x=3/2; locus of S3's centre is a parabola; power minimised at y0=0.
questions.justification: Combines radical axes, a focus-directrix locus and a minimisation over a parameter; the idea that P is free on a line and the extremum is at its foot is not routine.

questions.key_step: Split x^2/(1+x^2)=1-1/(1+x^2), integrate the periodic part exactly, bound the remainder by 1/2<=f<=1.
questions.justification: Periodic-integral evaluation plus a sandwich estimate and option comparison; two well-known ideas linked, no heavy computation.

questions.key_step: Chord of contact is a family through the pole of L; circumcentre is midpoint of OP; midpoint of AB is inverse of P.
questions.justification: Four statements, each a standard pole-polar fact but each needing its own derivation (loci especially); single chapter.

questions.key_step: x^(2n) limit gives the pieces; the join at +-1 is C1 but not C2; LMVT uniqueness needs the sign of f'.
questions.justification: Four statements across limits, differentiability, series and MVT; each needs a genuine check and the unique-root claim needs care; multi-concept MCQ.

questions.key_step: Leibniz with limits +-x gives f'=x^2+cos x; then all four statements follow.
questions.justification: One familiar move (Leibniz or the even-function pairing) and four quick consequences; routine but multi-concept MCQ so the 2.5 floor applies.

questions.key_step: Inverse-function derivatives g',g'',g''' at x=1, then the determinant reduces to g^3-2gg'+g''.
questions.justification: Needs inverse derivatives up to the third order and then D'(4) with careful arithmetic; each statement is a check with no options to eliminate.

questions.key_step: Parametric differentiation twice: f=t^4/2 then df/dx=(t^2+1)^2.
questions.justification: Long-looking but routine parametric chain; simplifications are designed to factor nicely.

questions.key_step: dg/dx=(t^2+1)^2-e^2>0 and transfer t>sqrt(e-1) to x>x(sqrt(e-1))=1/e.
questions.justification: Builds on Q9; needs the monotone map t->x and one evaluation; short but needs the paragraph's result.

questions.key_step: Differentiate implicitly twice at the origin.
questions.justification: Two implicit differentiations with a product/chain rule; routine multi-step with no insight.

questions.key_step: y^2-[y]^2-{y}^2=2[y]{y} makes Phi=Psi=x{1/x}->0+, then a 1^inf limit.
questions.justification: The GIF/FPF identity is the non-obvious step, followed by a standard 1^inf evaluation.

questions.key_step: Recognise e^x(u+u') and v+xv'=(xv)' to collapse g to x ln x+2x^2+2.
questions.justification: Recognising a hidden product-rule form in the second integral is a rarely practised idea; the rest is short.

questions.key_step: Lines 2 apart give R=1; chord of contact passes through the pole of L3.
questions.justification: Needs the pole of a line idea after setting up the geometry; moderate chain with one standard but non-trivial concept.

questions.key_step: Piecewise form of max{x,min{x^2,2-x^2}} and slope comparison at the switches.
questions.justification: Routine envelope analysis with one trap (x=1 is not a corner); several steps but no insight.

questions.key_step: Inflection at x=1; angle between tangents.
questions.justification: Standard inflection point and angle-between-curves formula; three routine steps.

questions.key_step: Area of CAPB = R*sqrt(CP^2-R^2), least at the foot of the perpendicular.
questions.justification: Standard tangent-length and minimum-distance chain; three routine steps.
